title: Kissed French Onions Tarte Tatin
description: A light, Burgundy-inspired Tarte Tatin featuring sweet and mustardy French onions, perfect for a brunch gathering.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine onions, thyme, bay leaves, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat.
Melt 2 tablespoons of butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion mixture and cook, stirring occasionally, until caramelized and golden brown, about 25-30 minutes.
Stir in mustard and cook for an additional 2 minutes.
Roll out the almond flour dough to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Transfer the dough to a hot stone plate or a 9-inch tart pan with a removable bottom, pressing it into the corners and edges.
Arrange the caramelized onion mixture evenly over the dough, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Arrange the apple slices on top of the onion mixture, slightly overlapping them.
In a small bowl, whisk together eggs and a pinch of salt. Brush the egg mixture over the apples, making sure to get some on the edges of the dough.
Dollop the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter on top of the apples.
Bake the Tarte Tatin for 25-30 minutes, or until the apples are tender and the edges of the crust are golden brown.
Remove from oven and let cool for 10 minutes before serving.
Loosen the edges of the Tarte Tatin with a knife or spatula, then invert onto a serving plate.
Serve warm, garnished with fresh thyme if desired.
This Tarte Tatin is best served immediately, but it can be refrigerated for up to a day and reheated in the oven before serving.
For a crispy crust, bake the Tarte Tatin at 425°F (220°C) for the first 10 minutes, then reduce the heat to 375°F (190°C) and continue baking for the remaining 15-20 minutes.
